insight: Both 1 Peter 5:7 and Psalm 55:22 use the imperative to cast or throw burdens decisively onto God, emphasizing an active transfer of anxiety or difficulties to Him. Each verse assures believers of God's personal care and sustaining power—Peter highlights God's ongoing, personal concern ('he careth for you'), while the Psalm affirms God's provision and protection, promising that the righteous will not be permanently shaken. Peter explicitly echoes the Psalm's principle, grounding Christian trust in God's faithful care amid trials.
